techniques.title: Dedicated Identity / Isolated Operating Profile
techniques.what_it_does: The agent operates under a purpose-built identity with minimum roles, isolated cookies, no saved personal credentials, and approved applications only — never inside the owner's personal browser session.
techniques.why_it_works: It collapses the attack surface: a compromised or misbehaving agent cannot reach what its identity cannot see.
techniques.genesis_implementation: The station module (hardware/environment probing) should enforce a GENESIS-only OS user profile on the Windows body: separate credentials vault, no access to the father's personal browser sessions, allowlisted applications. Document this as a Birth-Test checklist item.

techniques.title: Consent-First Trust Architecture
techniques.what_it_does: Avatar creation requires a verified consent video; voice cloning requires an in-product consent acknowledgment with explicit authorization statements; enterprise accounts are excluded from model training by default; the platform holds SOC 2 Type II and GDPR certifications and prepares for EU AI Act transparency obligations.
techniques.why_it_works: Consent is captured at the moment of highest leverage — before the artifact exists — rather than enforced through terms of service after the fact. This converts an abuse problem into a workflow gate.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Wire consent capture into the avatar host's enrollment flow as a hard gate (no consent artifact → no training). Log provenance for every identity and every render. This aligns with our own verification-first laws.

techniques.title: Provenance and Compliance Stack (machine-readable proof)
techniques.what_it_does: The platform ships C2PA content credentials and AI labels with every video (machine-readable proof of origin that travels with the file), holds SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, ISO 42001 (first AI video company to achieve it) and GDPR compliance, maintains a dedicated Trust & Safety team, participates in the Content Authenticity Initiative, and honors data-deletion requests from depicted persons.
techniques.why_it_works: Compliance is the enterprise buying criterion. C2PA credentials make provenance verifiable by machines, not just promised in marketing. ISO 42001 specifically addresses AI management systems — the standard that matters when a tool generates synthetic media of employees.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Every artifact the GENESIS build pipeline produces should carry provenance metadata (source, engine version, consent reference, timestamp) in a machine-readable envelope — our own C2PA-style practice. This directly serves our verification-first laws (VERIFY-BEFORE-REPORT): an artifact without provenance is not shippable.

techniques.title: Open-Weight Core + Self-Hostability (data sovereignty)
techniques.what_it_does: Fish Speech / S1-mini weights are published open-source, so teams can self-host the models in their own VPC or air-gapped environments when data residency matters. The hosted API and the open weights coexist as two tiers of the same product.
techniques.why_it_works: Voice data is sensitive. For the father's own voice — the one voice GENESIS will speak with — the recording and the embedding should never have to leave his device. Open weights make "your voice never leaves your hardware" a real architecture, not a promise.
techniques.genesis_implementation: STRONG RECOMMENDATION for the voice module: default to a self-hosted/local inference path for the father's voice (station module owns the local runtime). Cloud API is a fallback the father must explicitly enable per case. Enrollment recordings and embeddings live on-device; sync only with his approval.

prompt_patterns.title: Reference Clip Curation (one clip, one voice, finished sentence)
prompt_patterns.pattern: 15–30 seconds of clean speech, one microphone, one room, consistent energy. The clip's transcript must be EXACT (word-for-word), because the reference tokens anchor on it. End the clip on a finished sentence — a mid-sentence cut makes the clone leak the last word onto the start of every generated line. One reference per voice; reuse the same reference for every line of a session.
prompt_patterns.template: > Record → transcribe verbatim → trim to the last complete sentence → > check single-speaker, no overlap, no background music → register as the > voice's reference. Noisy room? Shorter and quieter beats longer and > noisier.

workflows.title: Voice Enrollment (cloning the father's voice)
workflows.body:
The identity-gated onboarding for the one voice GENESIS will speak with.
Local/self-hosted path preferred (T-13).

1. **CONSENT** — The father records a spoken consent phrase (his voice, his
   words, naming the purpose: personal assistant). Stored with timestamp;
   required before anything else. Entry: explicit request to enroll a
   voice. Exit: consent recording exists, or the workflow stops
   (fail-closed).
2. **SAMPLE** — Record enrollment audio: 15–30 seconds of natural speech
   (P-05), one microphone, one room, consistent energy; transcribed
   verbatim; trimmed to the last complete sentence. Entry: consent on file.
   Exit: single-speaker, clean sample (no overlap, no background noise, no
   music), or re-record.
3. **REGISTER** — Encoder extracts reference tokens; the voice record is
   created with tier=instant, consent reference, scope, and
   visibility=private (P-07). Exit: voice_id usable in any TTS call
   immediately.
4. **VERIFY** — Generate 3 test phrases (greeting, father's name, one
   acronym like "YPP"); the father listens and approves. Entry: registered
   voice_id. Exit: father approval, or return to SAMPLE with notes.
5. **PROMOTE (optional, deep tier)** — If instant fidelity is insufficient
   for daily use: longer clean session, trained clone, father's explicit
   per-case approval. Exit: tier=trained, QC'd on a long passage before
   activation.

Failure modes guarded:
| Failure | Guard |
|---|---|
| Cloning someone else's voice | Consent recording IS the speaker's voice; mismatch = abort |
| Bad sample → bad clone forever | VERIFY stage listens before any real use |
| Voice shared publicly by default | Visibility defaults to private; public is an explicit logged opt-in |
| Enrollment data leaves the device | Local path default; cloud fallback needs father's per-case approval |
| Voice used beyond consent scope | Consent names the purpose; new purpose = new consent |

techniques.title: Soul ID: Train-Once Identity Lock
techniques.what_it_does: A persona is trained once from a set of reference photos (~20 consistent portraits, ideally multi-angle: front, side, 3/4 via a composite sheet) into a persistent identity profile. Every later generation references that profile by name; the same face appears across shots, models, and sessions without re-uploading references.
techniques.why_it_works: Per-shot reference images drift over a long series (references of references). A trained profile is a stable embedding: one source of truth for identity, versioned once, consumed everywhere.
techniques.genesis_implementation: For the station/eyes modules and the 369 content library: build an `identity_profiles/` store — a named identity = one folder with canonical reference images + a fixed descriptor block (face, build, wardrobe, palette HEXes). Any asset pipeline that reuses a persona loads the profile by ID; regenerating the identity requires a versioned change, never a silent drift. Keep a profile-change log so a face that "changes" is always traceable to a deliberate edit.

techniques.title: Grid Generation + Composite Reference Sheet (pre-training consistency)
techniques.what_it_does: Generate the character with 2x2/4x4 grid variations, capture front/side/3-4 angles (3D orbit mode), arrange the best angles into a single composite reference sheet, and upload THAT as the identity reference. Multi-angle sheets dramatically improve consistency across extreme angle changes and profile views.
techniques.why_it_works: A single reference photo under-constrains the face in 3D; the model must invent what the profile looks like. A composite sheet gives it the profile, the three-quarter, the front — invention is replaced with reference.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Standardize the identity-profile folder (T-03): it must contain the multi-angle composite sheet, not a single photo, before a character is "locked". The profile-lock gate checks for ≥3 angles + the descriptor block. techniques.title: Deterministic Hooks: Steer vs. Enforce Split
techniques.what_it_does: Lifecycle hooks (shell commands triggered on events like before-tool-use, after-tool-use, or agent-stop) with matchers on the tool or action. A hook's exit code can hard-block an action regardless of what the model decided; anything written to stderr becomes the model's feedback. Anthropic's own guidance draws the line: prompting is a request, a hook is a guarantee — the model choosing to run a formatter is different from the formatter running automatically.
techniques.why_it_works: Instructions can be ignored under pressure or fade over long sessions. A deterministic check blocks regardless of the model's judgment, which is the only real enforcement layer in an agentic system.
techniques.genesis_implementation: This is the pattern our hands permission_gate must fully adopt: advisory rules live in prompts; hard blocks live in hook-equivalent deterministic code checks (protect paths, deny secret exfiltration, refuse destructive ops). Every law we consider load-bearing gets a deterministic check, not just a sentence in the system prompt. Warn-only on stop events (blocking there risks loops); hard-block on pre-action events.

techniques.title: Emphasis-Calibrated Instruction Design
techniques.what_it_does: On strong instruction-following models, aggressive emphasis (CAPS, MUST, CRITICAL) is dialed back because it causes overtriggering — the model fires the rule where it doesn't apply. Preferred form: plain instruction plus a reason ("Use this tool when… because…"). Extra guardrails are added only after an observed failure, not by default; safety gates stay unconditional but reason-anchored.
techniques.why_it_works: Over-emphasis creates false triggers and warning noise that gets ignored; reason-anchored instructions hold gates without saturating the agent. Observed-failure guardrails keep the prompt lean.
techniques.genesis_implementation: A system-prompt style guide for every module: reasons on every standing instruction, no bare CAPS imperatives, guardrail log of observed failures that earned their line. techniques.raw:
- **What it does:** On strong instruction-following models, aggressive emphasis
  (CAPS, MUST, CRITICAL) is dialed back because it causes overtriggering — the
  model fires the rule where it doesn't apply. Preferred form: plain
  instruction plus a reason ("Use this tool when… because…"). Extra guardrails
  are added only after an observed failure, not by default; safety gates stay
  unconditional but reason-anchored.
- **Why it works:** Over-emphasis creates false triggers and warning noise that
  gets ignored; reason-anchored instructions hold gates without saturating the
  agent. Observed-failure guardrails keep the prompt lean.
- **GENESIS implementation:** A system-prompt style guide for every module:
  reasons on every standing instruction, no bare CAPS imperatives, guardrail
  log of observed failures that earned their line. Review prompts on the same
  schedule as code review — prompt bloat is a bug.

## Capability signals: vendor claims vs. independent evidence

| Capability | Vendor / official signal | Independent evidence |
|---|---|---|
| SWE-bench Verified (code repair) | Opus 4.6: 80.8%; Sonnet 4.6: 79.6% (Anthropic system card) | Compiled reports: Opus 4.7 ~87.6%; GPT-5.5's higher score carries a memorization asterisk per Anthropic's own decontamination analysis — treat leaderboard numbers as harness- and dataset-dependent |
| Terminal-Bench 2.0 (terminal agents) | Sonnet 4.6: 59.1%; Opus 4.6: 65.4% (system card) | Independent comparison: harness choice alone shifts scores 10+ points — the harness is as load-bearing as the model |
| OSWorld (computer use) | Sonnet 4.6: 72.5%; Opus 4.6: 72.7% (system card) | Community comparison: Claude beats GPT-5.3-Codex by ~8.5 pts on GUI navigation tasks — Claude's edge is real on visual/desktop work |
| Long-context retrieval (MRCR v2) | Opus 4.6: 76.0% (system card) | Sonnet 4.6: 51.2% — retrieval strength is tier-dependent, not a family trait; size the model to the retrieval workload |
| Multi-agent research lift | BrowseComp single 74.01% → multi-agent 82.07% (system-card digest) | Practitioner pattern corroborates: parallel researchers + condensed summaries reliably beat single-agent on synthesis tasks |
| Parallel subagent scale | Up to 20 parallel subagents, 3 nesting layers (docs) | Traffic analysis by practitioners: ~92 model calls in 13 min with up to 7 parallel subagents observed on a real fix |
| Pricing | Official price list | Third-party verified Oct 11 2026: Sonnet 5.5 $2/$10, Opus 5.5 $4/$20, Haiku 5.5 $0.10/$0.50 (≤100K prompt); prompt-cache reads up to 90% off; batch 50% off; no long-context surcharge on 4.6+ |
| Thinking redaction | Anthropic: redaction hides reasoning from UI only, no reasoning loss | AMD AI head reported performance decline correlated with the redaction rollout — contested by Anthropic, unresolved; lesson: never treat vendor explanation as the final word (our LAW-050) |
| Sycophancy / instruction fade | Anthropic's own research papers document RLHF-driven sycophancy | Practitioners report: standing instructions fade over long sessions; completion bias (claims without proof); task fraud (reporting done without doing) — all independently observed |
| 1M context window | Standard on 4.6+ at standard pricing | Verified in pricing compilations; retrieval quality at 1M is the open question, not the window size |

**Standing rule derived:** vendor numbers are the ceiling claim; independent
re-review is the floor we build on. Same discipline as the Astra pack's
ARC-AGI-3 lesson.

prompt_patterns.title: Because-Clause Constraints
prompt_patterns.use_when: writing any standing instruction or guardrail.
prompt_patterns.pattern: Never a bare prohibition; always the prohibition plus its reason. Reasons hold gates; bare imperatives cause false triggers.
prompt_patterns.template: > <Rule>, because <what breaks if it is violated and who pays the cost>. > Example shape: "Write tests before claiming a fix, because an untested fix > is a guess and a guess that ships becomes my bug."
prompt_patterns.raw:
- **Use when:** writing any standing instruction or guardrail.
- **Pattern:** Never a bare prohibition; always the prohibition plus its reason.
  Reasons hold gates; bare imperatives cause false triggers.
- **Template:**
  > <Rule>, because <what breaks if it is violated and who pays the cost>.
  > Example shape: "Write tests before claiming a fix, because an untested fix
  > is a guess and a guess that ships becomes my bug."

techniques.title: Checkpoint Snapshots with Full Rollback
techniques.what_it_does: Every agent work unit is captured as a checkpoint that restores files, agent memory, task state, and optionally the development database. Rollback returns the whole project to any earlier checkpoint. Database recovery windows are plan-dependent (e.g., days of point-in-time restore on higher tiers).
techniques.why_it_works: Autonomous agents make wrong turns; without cheap undo, the operator is forced to let a runaway build continue or lose everything. A checkpoint converts "the agent ruined it" into a two-click recovery, which is what makes long unattended runs psychologically affordable.
techniques.genesis_implementation: In the hands + station modules, snapshot the workspace (file tree hash + job state + memory diff) before every mutation stage of an app build. Expose `rollback(checkpoint_id)` in the scheduler. Critical edge case learned from Replit postmortems: code rollback and data rollback are INDEPENDENT axes — restoring files does not restore data and vice versa, so GENESIS snapshots must cover both and the rollback UI must say which axes it restores.

techniques.title: Unified Infrastructure Provisioning (one agent, whole stack)
techniques.what_it_does: The same agent that writes the code also provisions the database (dev and production separated), manages auth, stores secrets encrypted, configures object storage, and handles deployment — no separate DevOps step, no context handoff between "the coder" and "the deployer."
techniques.why_it_works: Every handoff is a context-loss event. One agent holding the full stack means the deploy configuration is derived from the same understanding as the code, which is why one-click deploy actually works for standard stacks.
techniques.genesis_implementation: When GENESIS builds for the father (landing pages, tools), the build job must include infrastructure artifacts from the same run: deploy config, secrets handling, and environment separation (dev vs prod). A build deliverable is not "complete" until it ships with its deployment recipe. Relevant to the GENESIS package sales track.

workflows.title: Publish Pipeline (preview → live with safeguards)
workflows.body:
For: shipping a finished build to a live URL.

1. **PRE-FLIGHT** — Run the full self-test on the preview (W-01 step 4)
   plus security basics: no secrets in code, auth enforced where required,
   error handling present on key paths.
   Exit: all green; secrets audit clean.
   Failure guard: any secret found in code blocks publish — the key must be
   moved to the secrets manager first.
2. **DEPLOY-TYPE SELECTION** — Declare the deployment type against the
   workload (T-13): static / autoscale / always-on / scheduled.
   Exit: type chosen with its cost implication stated.
   Failure guard: "just publish it" without a declared type is rejected.
3. **PUBLISH** — Deploy; separate production data from development data.
   Exit: live URL issued.
4. **LIVE VERIFY** — Run the key user flow against the LIVE URL, not the
   preview (P-10).
   Exit: live flow works, monitoring/logs reachable.
   Failure guard: live-broken-but-preview-fine routes to W-02 with the
   deployment logs, and the known rollback axis gap is respected: code
   rollback and data rollback are handled as independent operations (T-04).
5. **WATCH** — Usage dashboard, spend, and error logs checked at +1h and
   +24h after publish.
   Exit: no anomalies, spend within budget.
   Failure guard: spend spike or error storm triggers an immediate pause of
   the deployment and a human alert (T-14).

techniques.title: Declarative Assistant Packaging (Custom GPTs)
techniques.what_it_does: A complete assistant is declared as a data record: identity (name, description, avatar), system instructions, knowledge files, capability toggles, external actions, conversation starters, and visibility. The builder guides creation conversationally, then exposes a Configure tab for direct control, a live Preview panel for testing, and a save/share step.
techniques.why_it_works: It turns "prompt" into "product": one reusable, testable, shareable unit instead of re-typed context per session. The conversational builder lowers the floor; the Configure tab raises the ceiling; Preview shortens the feedback loop.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Define a GENESIS "assistant pack" schema in code (station + memory): name, charter, instruction file, knowledge bundle, tool allowlist, tool contracts, starter prompts, test script, version. Ship a pack-builder flow mirroring Create → Configure → Preview → Save: generate from a natural-language description, refine the config directly, run the test script in a sandbox, then publish to the internal pack registry.

techniques.title: Two-Field Custom Instructions
techniques.what_it_does: Personalization is split into exactly two fields: "what to know about you" (facts: role, domain, tools, constraints) and "how to respond" (format, tone, anti-patterns). Each is length-capped; the two are injected as system-role context on every message.
techniques.why_it_works: The split prevents the two classic failures: identity soup (facts mixed with style rules, both weakened) and prompt bloat (templates warn: treat the limit as a constraint, don't fill it). System-role weight makes them durable rules rather than requests.
techniques.genesis_implementation: The station module's father-profile should carry exactly two fields — `context` (facts: identity, projects, tools, standing laws) and `behavior` (format/tone rules, forbidden patterns) — with per-field char budgets. Inject as system context on every agent job. Add a trim-and- retest loop: when outputs drift, shrink instructions rather than grow them.

techniques.title: Conversation Starters (assistant onboarding)
techniques.what_it_does: Each custom assistant shows 2–4 suggested opening prompts that demonstrate its intended use cases. They are written by the builder, not generated.
techniques.why_it_works: A blank chat box is a blank page — most users underuse assistants because they don't know what to ask first. Starters are the builder's way of teaching the interface.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Every assistant pack (T-01) and every Project (T-03) carries starter prompts in the father's language. They must reflect the assistant's real configured abilities (no aspirational starters — that's a fabrication vector).

workflows.title: Custom Assistant Setup (Create → Configure → Preview → Save)
workflows.body:
Modeled on the public GPT Builder workflow. Builds a reusable assistant pack
(T-01).

1. **DESCRIBE** — Father states the job in plain words. The system drafts a
   pack: name, charter, instructions, capability needs. (P-01, P-02)
   Exit: a draft pack record exists with all fields filled.
2. **CONFIGURE** — Father (or an agent) edits the configuration directly:
   identity, instructions, knowledge bundle, tool allowlist + contracts,
   starters. (T-04, P-04)
   Exit: config is complete; every tool has a validated contract + behavior
   note; starters are all answerable.
3. **PREVIEW** — Run the pack's test script against realistic prompts,
   including edge cases and instruction conflicts, in a sandbox.
   Exit: all test prompts pass; no tool called outside its contract.
4. **SAVE** — Version, publish to the pack registry with visibility
   (private by default). Record charter version.
   Exit: versioned pack retrievable by name; audit entry written.
5. **REVIEW LOOP** — Corrections update the pack config (P-09-style
   preference learning), re-running PREVIEW before re-save.
   Exit: config and tests green again.

Guarded failure modes: aspirational starters (rejected at PREVIEW), unvalidated
tool contracts (blocked at CONFIGURE), silent visibility changes (all shares
logged).
